summary: Caraiani and Scholze prove that for the non-compact quasi-split unitary Shimura varieties X_K of U(n, n) over a CM field F with F^+ ≠ Q, the F_ℓ-cohomology localized at a Hecke eigensystem m lies in degrees ≥ d and the compactly supported one in degrees ≤ d, d = dim_C X_K, provided ρ_m has length at most 2 and is generic (unramified, no eigenvalue ratio p) at some prime p split completely in F (Theorem 1.1); the integral and non-Eisenstein refinements follow (Remarks 1.5–1.6), and this is the vanishing input of the potential automorphy theorems of [ACC+23]. The method extends the compact paper's Hodge–Tate period map approach to the minimal and toroidal compactifications: they construct partial minimal and toroidal compactifications of central leaves and of perfect Igusa varieties, prove the former affine, identify the fibres of π*_HT and π^tor_HT with them up to canonical compactification, prove semiperversity of the nearby cycles on the good-reduction locus, compute the Galois representations attached to Igusa cohomology through Shin's trace formula, base change and the twisted trace formula (where F^+ ≠ Q excludes cuspidal subgroups), and compute the boundary of the partial minimal compactification of Igusa varieties by a version of Pink's formula. The atlas's roadmap IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration is planned from this paper and plans nearly every item; the flag-variety Newton stratification it quotes from the compact paper goes to BunGAndNewtonStrata. Twelve misprints are recorded.

items.name: The locally symmetric spaces X_K and the Hecke algebra T^S (§1.0.1)
items.statement: F a CM field containing an imaginary quadratic F_0, F = F^+·F_0; V = F^{2n} with the split skew-hermitian form ⟨x, y⟩ = Σ_{i≤n}(x_iȳ_{2n+1−i} − x_{2n+1−i}ȳ_i), (x, y) = tr_{F/Q}⟨x, y⟩ and a self-dual O_F-lattice L; G(R) = {g ∈ GL_{O_F}(L)(R) : (gv, gw) = (v, w)} is quasi-split with G_R = U(n, n)^{[F^+:Q]}; X_K = G(Q)\(X × G(A_f)/K) of complex dimension d = [F^+:Q]n^2, whose Borel–Serre boundary contains locally symmetric spaces of GL_n/F; T = T^S = ⊗_{p∉S, p∈Spl_{F_0/Q}} Z[G(Q_p)//G(Z_p)] with the operators T_{i,v}.
items.note: IG's README fixes exactly this datum, level and Hecke algebra.

items.name: Galois representations attached to torsion eigensystems
items.statement: For m ⊂ T in the support of H^*(X_K, F_ℓ) there is a continuous semisimple ρ_m : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_{2n}(F̄_ℓ), unramified outside S, with the characteristic polynomial of ρ_m(Frob_v) the reduction of X^{2n} − T_{1,v}X^{2n−1} + … + (−1)^iq_v^{i(i−1)/2}T_{i,v}X^{2n−i} + … + q_v^{n(2n−1)}T_{2n,v}; likewise for torsion classes of GL_m/F, m ≤ n.
items.note: [Sch15, Thm 4.3.1, Cor. 5.4.3] and [ACC+23, Thms 2.3.3, 2.3.5] (via Shin's base change [Shi14]). IG's README names TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure and IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants as suppliers of these lower-rank torsion systems.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (the generic part of cohomology sits on the correct side of the middle degree)
items.statement: Assume (i) F^+ ≠ Q; (ii) ρ_m has length at most 2; (iii) some prime p ≠ ℓ splits completely in F and for all v | p, ρ_m is unramified at v with the eigenvalues α_{i,v} of ρ_m(Frob_v) satisfying α_{i,v} ≠ pα_{j,v} for i ≠ j. Then (1) H^i(X_K, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0 implies i ≥ d, and (2) H^i_c(X_K, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0 implies i ≤ d.
items.note: IG.7 proves exactly these inequalities. Remark 1.4: (iii) drops [CS17]'s condition α_i ≠ α_j, which Koshikawa observed to be superfluous also in [CS17].

items.name: Remarks 1.5–1.6 (integral consequences and the non-Eisenstein case)
items.statement: Under Theorem 1.1, the same holds for Z_ℓ-coefficients, H^d(X_K, Z_ℓ)_m is torsion-free, and 0 → H^{d−1}(∂X_K, Z_ℓ)_m → H^d_c(X_K, Z_ℓ)_m → H^d(X_K, Z_ℓ)_m → H^d(∂X_K, Z_ℓ)_m → 0 is exact; nontrivial coefficient systems V_λ follow by Hochschild–Serre. If ρ_m is absolutely irreducible, H^i_c(X_K, F_ℓ)_m ≅ H^i(X_K, F_ℓ)_m vanish outside i = d, and the same holds integrally with torsion-free H^d.
items.note: IG.7: the integral and local-system versions, the boundary exact sequence and the absolutely irreducible specialization ([ACC+23, Thm 2.4.2]).

items.name: Proposition 1.8 and Theorem 1.11 (compactified Igusa varieties and the fibres of the period map)
items.statement: The Γ_X-torsor Ig^X → C^X_perf extends uniquely to Ig^{X,tor} → C^{X,tor}_perf, isogeny-invariant when the isogeny is an isomorphism on étale quotients; Ig^{X,*} and C^{X,*} are affine (Proposition 1.9); the maps Ig^{X,tor}_C → (π^tor_HT)^{-1}(x) and Ig^{X,*}_C → (π*_HT)^{-1}(x) are open immersions of perfectoid spaces with the same rank-one points, the targets being the canonical compactifications.
items.note: Stated in the introduction; proved as Theorems 3.2.8, 3.3.2, 4.1.1 (items below). IG.2–IG.3.

items.name: The unitary similitude group G, the unitary group G^0 and Lemma 2.1.1
items.statement: G(R) = {(g, c) ∈ GL_{O_F}(L)(R) × G_m(R) : (gv, gw) = c(v, w)}, X = ∏X_{τ,+} ⊔ ∏X_{τ,−}, X_K; G^0 ⊂ G the unitary group, X^0_{K^0}; the Hecke operators T^0_{i,v}, T_{i,v} and the restriction T^S → T^{0,S}. For K^0 = K ∩ G^0(A_f), X^0_{K^0} → X_K is an open and closed immersion, Hecke-equivariant for T^S → T^{0,S} on H and H_c.
items.note: IG.0: 'the comparison between the unitary subgroup G^0 and the similitude group G' (CSnc §2.1).

items.name: Proposition 2.1.2 (the Hasse principle for G)
items.statement: H^1(Q, G) → ∏_v H^1(Q_v, G) is injective; equivalently, a 2n-dimensional F-vector space with an F-hermitian alternating form locally isomorphic to V up to scalars everywhere is isomorphic to V up to a scalar.
items.note: G^der is simply connected and G/G^der ≅ Res_{F^+/Q}T × G_m ([Kot92, §7]). The statement lets v run over 'all places of F' (sourceIssues E1). Part of IG.0's comparison of §2.1.

items.name: Definitions 2.1.3–2.1.5 and Proposition 2.1.6 (the moduli problem S_K)
items.statement: Abelian varieties and p-divisible groups with G-structure (O_F-action with Lie algebra free of rank n over O_F ⊗ O_S, principal polarization with Rosati involution = conjugation); S^pre_K over Z[1/Δ_F] with level-N structures liftable modulo Δ_F^mN for all m (a DM stack, representable away from Δ_F N or over Z_(p) when the prime-to-p part of N is ≥ 3); S_K its normalization in S^pre_K × Z[1/Δ_F N]; X_K ≅ S_K(C).
items.note: PELModuli M1–M3 own the PEL functor, representability and the complex comparison; IG.0 instantiates them for this datum.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.1 (splitting symplectic filtrations)
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, a p-divisible group with G-structure splits uniquely as X^µ ⊕ X^{(0,1)} ⊕ X^ét; more generally an O_F-stable filtration Z_{−2} ⊂ Z_{−1} ⊂ X with Z_{−2} multiplicative, X/Z_{−1} étale and Z_{−2} ≅ (X/Z_{−1})^∨ via λ splits O_F-linearly and symplectically.
items.note: IG.0 (PEL p-divisible groups; the motivation is the Igusa cusp labels of §3.3).

items.name: Proposition 2.2.3 and Theorem 2.2.4 (finite-level Igusa torsors over seminormal bases)
items.statement: For isoclinic X/k with EL or PEL structure, the liftable automorphisms Γ_m of X[p^m] form a finite étale group scheme representing liftable automorphisms fppf locally ([CS17, Cor. 4.1.10]). If X/k is seminormal and 𝒢/X is geometrically isomorphic to X everywhere, the liftable isomorphisms 𝒢[p^m] ×T ≅ X[p^m] × T form a Γ_m-torsor J_m(𝒢/X) → X.
items.note: Generalizes [Man05] from central leaves; via seminormality [Swa80, Thm 2.6], [CS17, L 4.3.15] and truncated Rapoport–Zink spaces. IG.0–IG.1.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.5 (points of a truncated Rapoport–Zink space with a fixed p-divisible group)
items.statement: For Y/k and the reduced special fibre M^{0,d}_Y of the truncated RZ space (isogenies with kernel in Y[p^d]), the locus where the universal group is geometrically isomorphic to Y consists of finitely many reduced points.
items.note: Generalizes [Man04, L 3.4]; [Oor04, Cor. 2.5]. IG.0 ('effectivity and algebraization of the relevant isomorphism functors').

items.name: Propositions 2.2.6–2.2.7 (Igusa torsors for non-isoclinic groups)
items.statement: For X perfect (resp. regular) and 𝒢 geometrically isomorphic to X, isomorphisms 𝒢 ×T ≅ X × T on perfect (resp. all) X-schemes form a torsor under the profinite group Γ = Aut(X)(k) (resp. the generally non-reduced group scheme Aut(X)).
items.note: IG.0: 'nonisoclinic Aut(X) need not be reduced'; IG.1 distinguishes the profinite torsor from the non-reduced one.

items.name: Central leaves and the perfect Igusa variety (Definition 2.3.1, Corollary 2.3.2)
items.statement: C^X = {x ∈ S_{K,k} : A[p^∞]_x̄ ≅ X_x̄ with G-structure}, locally closed and smooth with its reduced structure ([Man05, Prop. 1]); Ig^X → C^X is an Aut(X)-torsor, perfect, isogeny-invariant ([CS17, L 4.3.4]), giving correspondences C^X ← Ig^X ≅ Ig^{X'} → C^{X'}.
items.note: IG.0 (leaves as smooth subschemes) and IG.1 (Ig^X, perfectness, isogeny invariance).

items.name: Definition 2.3.3 and Lemma 2.3.4 (completely slope divisible p-divisible groups)
items.statement: 𝒢 over an F_p-scheme is isoclinic slope divisible of slope λ = r/s if p^{−r}Frob^s is an isomorphism, slope divisible w.r.t. λ if it is an isogeny, and completely slope divisible if it has a filtration with isoclinic slope-divisible graded pieces of strictly decreasing slopes; such filtrations are unique and fpqc local, and on a connected regular base complete slope divisibility at the generic point spreads out ([Zin01, Thm 7]).
items.note: IG.0: 'completely slope-divisible representatives after isogeny'.

items.name: Definition 2.3.5 and Remarks 2.3.6–2.3.7 (non-perfect Igusa varieties)
items.statement: For completely slope divisible X = ⊕X_i, the Igusa variety 𝔍𝔤^X → C^X of isomorphisms 𝒢^i ≅ X_i compatible with O_F ⊗ Z_p and the polarizations up to Z_p^×; its finite levels 𝔍𝔤^X_m are finite étale Galois with group Γ_{m,X}; 𝔍𝔤^X is pro-finite étale with group Γ_X, and Ig^X ≅ (𝔍𝔤^X)_perf ([CS17, Prop. 4.3.8]).
items.note: IG.1: 'smooth finite-level nonperfect models … identify their perfected limit with Ig^X'.

items.name: Theorems 2.4.1–2.4.2 (Serre–Tate for semi-abelian schemes)
items.statement: For S' → S surjective with nilpotent kernel and p nilpotent: p-divisible groups up to isogeny, abelian schemes up to p-power isogeny, and semi-abelian schemes that are global extensions of abelian schemes by split tori (with Hom[1/p]) deform uniquely; abelian schemes (resp. such extensions) over S' are equivalent to triples (A_S, 𝒢_{S'}, ρ : A_S[p^∞] ≅ 𝒢_{S'} × S).
items.note: Drinfeld's proof ([Kat81], [And03]) without noetherian hypotheses; [Mes72], [Ill85, Thm 4.4], [DG70, IX 3.6 bis]. IG.0: 'the Serre–Tate deformation and quasi-isogeny comparisons used in CSnc §§2.2–2.4'.

items.name: Degenerations over O_C and level structures at the boundary (§2.5.1)
items.statement: A principally polarized (A, λ) over C has a semi-abelian model with Raynaud extension 0 → T → G → B → 0, B principally polarized, character data f_0 : X → B and a symmetric lift f : X → G(C) with topologically nilpotent diagonal, A^an = G_η/X; with O_F-action X is a finite projective O_F-module; A[N] has the filtration T[N] ⊂ G[N] ⊂ A[N] and level structures correspond to data (1)–(3) subject to (2.5.2).
items.note: ShimuraCompactifications C4 (degenerations, 1-motives, level structures across boundary charts).

items.name: Cusp labels, the groups Γ_Z and the boundary Shimura varieties S_Z (§§2.5.2–2.5.3)
items.statement: A cusp label (Z, X): an O_F-stable symplectic filtration Z_{−2} ⊂ Z_{−1} ⊂ L ⊗ Ẑ with X ⊗ Ẑ ≅ Gr^Z_0; at level K a K-orbit (Definition 2.5.3); at K(N) pairs (Z_N, X); Γ_Z = {g ∈ GL_{O_F}(X) : g ≡ 1 mod N}; S_Z the unitary Shimura variety of the same type with n replaced by n − r, r = rk_{O_F}X.
items.note: ShimuraCompactifications C1/C5 and IG.2 (cusp labels at this level).

items.name: Cone decompositions (§2.5.4, Remarks 2.5.5–2.5.6)
items.statement: M_Z the space of O_F-hermitian forms on X ⊗ R, P^+_Z ⊂ P_Z (definite; semidefinite with F-rational radical), S_Z ⊂ M^∨_Z, rational polyhedral, smooth and nondegenerate cones, faces, Γ_Z-admissible decompositions Σ_Z, the order Z ≤ Z' with M_{Z'} ⊂ M_Z, compatible families; Σ may be chosen smooth, projective with trivial stabilizers ([Lan13, Def. 7.3.1.1, Prop. 7.3.1.4]).
items.note: ShimuraCompactifications C0 (admissible fans). The definition of Z ≤ Z' has its inclusions reversed (sourceIssues E2).

items.name: Theorem 2.5.8 (the minimal compactification)
items.statement: There is a flat projective normal S*_K over Z[1/NΔ_F] with a dense open S_K[1/N] ↪ S*_K, locally closed strata S_Z[1/N] for cusp labels with S_Z in the closure of S_{Z'} iff Z ≤ Z' (also fibrewise), and finite surjective Hecke maps [g] extending those of S_K.
items.note: [Lan13, §7], [Lan13, Def. 5.4.2.6], [LS18a, Rem. 4.3.3]. ShimuraCompactifications C5.

items.name: Theorem 2.5.9 (toroidal compactifications and their boundary charts)
items.statement: For Σ as above there is a projective S^tor_{K,Σ} over Z[1/Δ_F] with S_K dense open, smooth after inverting N, stratified by cusp labels Z and by (Z, [σ]), with formal completion along the Z-stratum ≅ 𝔛_{Z,Σ_Z}/Γ_Z (C_Z = Hom_{O_F}((1/N)X, B^∨) → S_Z abelian, Ξ_Z → C_Z a torsor under the torus with character group S_Z, relative torus embedding Ξ_Z ↪ Ξ_{Z,Σ_Z}), a semi-abelian scheme with Raynaud extension G_Z, closure relations by Z ≤ Z' and faces, the charts Ξ(σ) ⊃ Ξ_σ, and a projective π_{K,Σ} : S^tor[1/N] → S*_K with π_*O = O.
items.note: [Lan13, §§6–7], [LS18a, Rem. 2.1.8], and at primes dividing N the models of [Lan16]. ShimuraCompactifications C5 (integral PEL compactifications with higher p-level normalizations). Part (4) writes M_Z ⊆ M_{Z'} for M_{Z'} ⊆ M_Z (sourceIssues E3).

items.name: Definition 2.6.1 and Theorem 2.6.2 (perfectoid compactified Shimura varieties)
items.statement: S*_{K(p^∞N)} = lim S*^◇_{K(p^mN),Q_p} and S^tor_{K(p^∞N)} = lim S^tor^◇ as spatial diamonds over Spd Q_p ([Sch17, L 11.22]); S*_{K(p^∞N)} and (for cofinal Σ) S^tor_{K(p^∞N)} are representable by perfectoid spaces.
items.note: [Sch15, Thm 4.1.1] with [BS22, Thm 1.17(1)]; [PS16, Thm 0.4], [Lan22] and strongly Zariski closed subsets [BS22, Rem. 7.5], [Sch15, L 2.2.2]. S1–S2 and S6 plan the perfectoid towers and their compactifications.

items.name: Étale sheaves O^+/p on locally spatial diamonds and Remark 2.6.3
items.statement: A locally spatial diamond D over Spd Q_p has an étale sheaf O^+_D/p pulling back to O^+_{X♯}/p on quasi-pro-étale perfectoids ([Sch17, Thm 14.12(ii)]), agreeing with O^+_X/p for D = X^◇, and O^+_D/p = colim π_i^*O^+_{D_i}/p for cofiltered limits of spatial diamonds. Remark 2.6.3: density of finite-level functions [Sch15, Thm 4.1.1], [PS16, Thm 0.4]; for the minimal compactification this density is open.
items.note: DiamondEtaleCohomology C0 (sites of diamonds). Remark 2.6.3 notes that the density claimed in the original version of [SW20, Lecture X] was proved incorrectly.

items.name: Proposition 2.6.4 (the good-reduction locus carries all the cohomology)
items.statement: For C algebraically closed over Q_p and N ≥ 3, H^i(S_{K(N),Q̄}, F_ℓ) → H^i(S°_{K(N),C}, F_ℓ) is a Hecke-equivariant isomorphism, S° ⊂ S the locus of good reduction.
items.note: Lan–Stroh [LS18b], [LS18a, Cor. 5.20] and [Hub96, Thm 3.5.13]. IG.3 plans the Lan–Stroh nearby-cycle comparison and the good-reduction open part.

items.name: Theorem 2.7.1 (the Hodge–Tate period map on the minimal compactification)
items.statement: There is a G(A_f)-equivariant π*_HT : S*_{K(p^∞N)} → Fℓ extending π°_HT on S°_{K(p^∞N)} (Fℓ the flag variety of totally isotropic F-linear subspaces of V), and π^tor_HT by composition.
items.note: [Sch15, Thm 4.1.1], [CS17, Thm 2.1.3] and [CGH+20, Thm 3.3.1]. S3 and S6 plan the period map and its extension to compactifications.

items.name: Theorem 2.7.2 (fibres over the good-reduction locus, from [CS17])
items.statement: For x ∈ Fℓ(C) with p-divisible group 𝒳_{O_C} ([SW13, Thm B]) and special fibre X_k, there is a canonical open immersion Ig^{X_k}_C ↪ (π°_HT)^{-1}(x) containing all rank-one points, and (Rπ°_HT*F_ℓ)_x ≅ RΓ(Ig^{X_k}, F_ℓ) Hecke-equivariantly.

items.name: Theorem 2.7.3 (the Newton stratification of Fℓ, from [CS17, §3])
items.statement: Fℓ = ⊔_{b∈B(G_{Q_p},µ^{-1})} Fℓ^b with locally closed partially proper strata, x ∈ Fℓ^b(C) iff b(x) = b, dim Fℓ^b = d − d_b with d_b = dim Ig^b = ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩ ([Ham15]), and Fℓ^{≥b} = ⊔_{b'≥b} Fℓ^{b'} closed.
items.note: The strata come from [CS17, §3] (modifications of G-bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve, routed by PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17 to BG2–BG3); IG.3 uses 'flag Newton strata' without constructing them. The order on B(G) is called 'the Bruhat order'.

items.name: The ordinary stratum
items.statement: As the reflex field is Q, the ordinary element is the largest of B(G_{Q_p}, µ^{-1}) ([Wed99, Thm 1.6.3]), and Fℓ^ord = Fℓ(Q_p) is 0-dimensional ([CGH+20, Prop. 3.3.8]).

items.name: Theorem 2.8.1 and Proposition 2.8.2 (affineness and Artin vanishing)
items.statement: The partial minimal compactification Ig^{b,*} is affine, so H^i_{c−∂}(Ig^b, F_ℓ) := H^i(Ig^{b,*}, j_!F_ℓ) vanishes for i > d_b = dim Ig^b.
items.note: IG.2 (affineness) and IG.4 (the upper bound for the partial-support complex).

items.name: Lemma 2.8.4 (the lower bound at a minimal Newton stratum)
items.statement: For m ⊂ T^S (S ⊃ {∞} ∪ primes dividing pℓNΔ_F) and b with d_b minimal among those with H^*(Ig^b, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0: H^i(Ig^b, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0 implies i ≥ d_b.
items.note: As [CS17, Cor. 6.1.4], without constructibility (perverse sheaves need not be constructible; overconvergence of qcqs pushforwards). IG.4.

items.name: Theorem 2.8.6 = Corollary 5.1.3 (Galois representations and the ordinary stratum)
items.statement: Assume F^+ ≠ Q and p split in F_0. If H^i(Ig^b, F_ℓ)_m is nonzero for exactly one i, there is a semisimple ρ_m : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_{2n}(F̄_ℓ) with the expected Frobenius characteristic polynomials at v | q ∉ S split in F_0; if moreover p splits completely in F, ρ_m is unramified at v | p and α_{i,v} ≠ pα_{j,v} for i ≠ j, then b is ordinary.
items.note: Via the dual ideal m^∨ = ι(m) [ACC+23, §2.2.11] and ρ_m := ρ_{m^∨}|Art_F^{-1}|^{1−2n}; generic principal series do not transfer to nontrivial inner forms ([CS17, L 5.4.3]); cases p ≢ 1 and p ≡ 1 mod ℓ (footnote 17). IG.5 proves this obstruction.

items.name: Theorem 2.8.7 = Theorem 6.4.1 (the boundary obstruction)
items.statement: Assume F^+ ≠ Q and p split in F_0. If H^i_{c−∂}(Ig^b, F_ℓ)_m or H^i(Ig^b, F_ℓ)_m is nonzero there is ρ_m as above, and if H^i_{c−∂}(Ig^b, F_ℓ)_m → H^i(Ig^b, F_ℓ)_m fails to be an isomorphism for some i with b not ordinary, then ρ_m has length at least 3.
items.note: IG.6 (the length obstruction of CSnc Theorem 2.8.7).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1 and the dual Hecke ideal
items.statement: Only the ordinary b contributes, so (Rπ°_HT*F_ℓ)_m lives on Fℓ(Q_p) in degrees ≥ d; Hochschild–Serre, Proposition 2.6.4, Lemma 2.1.1 and Proposition 2.1.6 give (1); Poincaré duality with m^∨ = ι(m), ι([K_SgK_S]) = [K_Sg^{-1}K_S] ([ACC+23, Prop. 2.2.12, Cor. 2.2.13]) and ρ_{m^∨} ≅ ρ_m^∨|Art_F^{-1}|^{1−2n} (Frob_v-eigenvalues p^{2n−1}α_{i,v}^{-1}) give (2).
items.note: IG.7 (and IG.5 for the dual ideal and characteristic-polynomial dictionary); R02.2 for Hochschild–Serre.

items.name: Definition 3.1.1 and Remark 3.1.2 (well-positioned subsets)
items.statement: A locally closed Y ⊆ S_k is well-positioned if there are locally closed Y^♮_Z ⊆ S_{Z,k} such that a point degenerating into Z lies in Y iff the base of its Raynaud extension lies in Y^♮_Z; this agrees with [LS18a, Def. 2.2.1] (via the covers 𝔛°_σ, (3.1.1)) and with [Box15, Def. 3.4.1], independently of Σ.
items.note: IG.2: 'Construct well-positioned subsets/subschemes using the actual formal toroidal charts'.

items.name: Partial compactifications and Proposition 3.1.3
items.statement: For well-positioned Y: Y^* := Ỹ^* ∖ Y^*_0 and Y^tor := Ỹ^tor ∖ Y^tor_0 ([LS18a, Thm 2.3.3]) with Y^* ×_{S*} S_Z = Y^♮_Z; if Y ⊂ Y' are well-positioned with Y closed in Y', then Y^* is closed in Y'^*.
items.note: IG.2.

items.name: Proposition 3.1.4 and Lemma 3.1.5 (leaves are well-positioned; smooth toroidal leaves)
items.statement: C^X is well-positioned, with (C^X)^♮_Z the leaf of the unique X_Z with X ≅ Hom(X, µ_{p^∞}) ⊕ X_Z ⊕ X ⊗ Q_p/Z_p (or empty); C^{X,tor} is smooth.
items.note: [LS18a, Props 3.4.2, 2.3.13]; IG.2: 'Prove central leaves are well-positioned'.

items.name: Propositions 3.2.1–3.2.2 (the connected part at the boundary)
items.statement: Over C^{X,tor}, A[p^∞]° (= Â[p^∞]) is a p-divisible group, geometrically ≅ X° = Hom(X, µ_{p^∞}) ⊕ X_Z°; its multiplicative part has constant rank and the polarization of the biconnected part A[p^∞]^{(0,1)} extends from C^X.
items.note: IG.2 (toroidal Igusa geometry).

items.name: Theorem 3.2.4, Definition 3.2.5 and Theorem 3.2.6 (finite-level toroidal Igusa varieties)
items.statement: For completely slope divisible X, 𝔍𝔤^X_m → C^X extends uniquely to a finite étale Γ_{m,X}-cover 𝔍𝔤^{X,tor}_m → C^{X,tor} representing Igusa level p^m structures on A[p^∞]^i (λ_i > 0); its completion along the Z-stratum is ≅ 𝔜_{Z,Σ_Z}/Γ_Z, built from the connected part H_Z of the Raynaud extension over C_Z ×_{S_Z} C^X_Z.
items.note: IG.2: 'formal boundary charts, torus embeddings, and quotients by cusp stabilizers'.

items.name: Theorem 3.2.8, Definition 3.2.9 and Remark 3.2.10 (perfect toroidal Igusa varieties)
items.statement: The pro-finite étale Γ_X-cover Ig^X → C^X_perf extends uniquely to Ig^{X,tor} → C^{X,tor}_perf, representing perfect Igusa level structures (A[p^∞]° ≅ X° with a scalar compatible on biconnected parts); Ig^X is an fpqc Aut(X)-torsor over C^X but not over the toroidal boundary ([How20, §3]).
items.note: IG.2: 'Extend the Γ_X torsor uniquely over (C^{X,tor})_perf'.

items.name: Propositions 3.2.11–3.2.12 and Theorem 3.2.13 (boundary charts of Ig^{X,tor})
items.statement: C^{Ig,X}_Z parametrizes (B, ι, λ, η) ∈ S_Z, a Raynaud extension 0 → T → G → B → 0 and an O_F-linear embedding ρ : G[p^∞] ↪ X with symplectic T[p^∞] ⊂ G[p^∞] ⊂ X and B[p^∞] ≅ Gr_{−1} compatibly with polarizations; Ξ^{Ig,X}_Z → C^{Ig,X}_Z is the perfection of the torsor of symmetric lifts f : X → G (equivalently X[1/p] → G after a splitting), and Îg^{X,tor}_Z ≅ 𝔜_{Z,Σ_Z}/Γ_Z.
items.note: IG.2 ('Build its explicit cusp labels, formal boundary charts').

items.name: Corollary 3.2.14 (isogeny invariance of the toroidal Igusa variety)
items.statement: An isogeny φ : X → X' of p-divisible groups with G-structure inducing isomorphisms on étale and multiplicative parts extends Ig^X ≅ Ig^{X'} uniquely to Ig^{X,tor} ≅ Ig^{X',tor}.
items.note: IG.2: isogeny invariance of the toroidal model 'keeps the required isomorphism on étale quotients'.

items.name: Theorem 3.3.2 and Lemma 3.3.3 (partial minimal compactifications of leaves are affine)
items.statement: C^{X,*} is affine: some leaf in the isogeny class lies in an Ekedahl–Oort stratum inside the Newton stratum ([Nie15, Prop. 1.5, Cor. 1.6]) whose partial minimal compactification is affine ([Box15, Thm C]); then transfer by isogenies and the lemma: in X_0 ⊂ X ← C → Y ⊃ Y_0 with C_0 the preimage of both, X, X_0, Y_0 affine and π_1, π_2 proper surjective and finite away from C_0, Y is affine.
items.note: IG.2 follows exactly this route (Ekedahl–Oort, Nie, Boxer, isogeny transfer).

items.name: Proposition 3.3.4, Definition 3.3.7 and Lemma 3.3.8 (partial minimal compactifications of Igusa varieties)
items.statement: Ig^{X,*}, the normalization of C^{X,*} in Ig^X, is integral over C^{X,*}, affine, equal to the Stein factorization of Ig^{X,tor} → C^{X,*} (Ig^{X,*} = Spec H^0(Ig^{X,tor}, O)) and isogeny-invariant; for completely slope divisible X_b, Ig^{b,*} → C^{b,*} is finite surjective and Ig^b ↪ Ig^{b,*} is dense open with Ig^{b,*} normal.
items.note: IG.2: 'Prove affineness of C^{X,*} and Ig^{X,*}'.

items.name: Definition 3.3.10 (Igusa cusp labels)
items.statement: Z̃ = (Z_b, Z^p, X): an O_F-stable filtration Z_{b,−2} ⊂ Z_{b,−1} ⊂ X_b with multiplicative Z_{b,−2}, étale X_b/Z_{b,−1}, Cartier dual via λ; a symplectic filtration Z^p of L ⊗ Ẑ^p; X finite projective over O_F with X ⊗ Q_p/Z_p ≅ Gr^{Z_b}_0, X ⊗ Ẑ^p ≅ Gr^{Z^p}_0; the action of J_b(Q_p) × G(A^p_f), levels, and at Γ_b(p^m)K^p(N) triples (Z_{m,b}, Z_N, X); Γ_Z̃.
items.note: IG.2: 'explicit cusp labels'.

items.name: Theorem 3.3.12 and Definition 3.3.13 (boundary strata of finite-level toroidal Igusa varieties)
items.statement: The completion of Ig^{b,tor}_m along the Z-stratum decomposes over Igusa cusp labels Z̃ above Z, and each piece is 𝔛_{Z̃,Σ_Z}/Γ_Z̃ for the abelian scheme C_Z̃ = Hom_{O_F}((1/N)X, (B/B[p^m]^µ)^∨) over the level-p^m Igusa variety Ig^b_{Z,m} of the boundary leaf, parametrizing Igusa structures compatible with Z̃ and a splitting δ_{m,b}.
items.note: IG.2.

items.name: Theorem 3.3.15 (boundary strata of Ig^{b,*}_m)
items.statement: Ig^{b,*}_m = ⊔_Z̃ Ig^b_Z̃ locally closed, with Ig^b_Z̃ ≅ Ig^b_{Z,m} the level-p^m Igusa variety over the leaf C^b_Z in the boundary stratum S_Z.
items.note: Stein factorization, Zariski's main theorem and Fourier–Jacobi arguments as in [Lan13, §7]; IG.2.

items.name: Theorem 4.1.1 and Corollary 4.1.2 (fibres of the compactified period maps)
items.statement: For x ∈ Fℓ(C) with p-divisible group 𝒳_{O_C} and α : T_p𝒳 ≅ L ⊗ Z_p, there are natural maps Ig^{X,*}_C → (π*_HT)^{-1}(x) and Ig^{X,tor}_C → (π^tor_HT)^{-1}(x), open immersions of perfectoid spaces with the same rank-one points whose targets are the canonical compactifications; hence RΓ(Ig^{X,*}, F_ℓ) ≅ (Rπ*_HT*F_ℓ)_x and RΓ(Ig^{X,tor}, F_ℓ) ≅ (Rπ^tor_HT*F_ℓ)_x Hecke-equivariantly, with higher-rank stalks equal to rank-one stalks.
items.note: IG.3 exports CSnc Theorem 4.1.1/Corollary 4.1.2.

items.name: Theorem 4.2.1 and Corollary 4.2.2 (the period map on boundary strata)
items.statement: On the completion Ŝ^tor_{K(p^∞N),Z} with its map to (G/P_r)(Q_p) and local system L_Z = Gr_{−1}, π^tor_HT is given by the Hodge–Tate filtration Lie B(1) ⊂ L_Z ⊗ O pulled back to Z_{p^∞,−1}; on a boundary stratum S_{K(p^∞N),Ẑ} of the minimal compactification, π*_HT is the period map of the smaller Shimura variety followed by Fℓ_Ẑ ↪ Fℓ.
items.note: [Sch15, Prop. 3.3.1] away from the boundary and a continuity argument. IG.3 constructs the maps respecting boundary filtrations.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.1 (the p-divisible group is constant modulo p^ε)
items.statement: There is ε ∈ Q ∩ (0, 1] and an isomorphism X ×_k O_C/p^ε ≅ 𝒳 ×_{O_C} O_C/p^ε with G-structures lifting the identity and matching the splittings δ.
items.note: [SW13, Thm A] and the classification of G-Dieudonné modules over B^+_cris by G-bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve ([Far20, Thms 5.1, 5.6]); IG.3 ('identify its polarized p-divisible group over O_C and special fiber X').

items.name: Theorem 4.3.2 (the map from compactified Igusa varieties to compactified Shimura varieties)
items.statement: The map g : Ig^X_{O_C} → S_{K(p^∞N),O_C} (Serre–Tate lift of the universal abelian scheme with its level structure from α) extends to g^tor : Ig^{X,tor}_{O_C} → S^tor_{K(p^∞N),O_C}, Ig^{X,tor}_{O_C} := W(Ig^{X,tor}) ×_{W(k)} O_C.
items.note: On boundary charts: deform G[p^∞] ↪ X, Serre–Tate for Raynaud extensions (Theorem 2.4.2), torus torsors of symmetric lifts, Igusa cusp labels ↦ cusp labels; agreement via vanishing cotangent complexes of relatively perfect lifts. IG.3.

items.name: Theorem 4.4.1 and Lemma 4.4.2 (the toroidal fibre and canonical compactifications)
items.statement: g^tor induces Ig^{b,tor}_C → (π^tor_HT)^{-1}(x), an open immersion with the same rank-one points; since the target is partially proper it is the canonical compactification. Lemma: a map from a quasicompact separated perfectoid X to a proper diamond Y over Spd C that is bijective on (C', O_{C'})-points for all C'/C identifies the canonical compactification of X with Y ([Sch17, Prop. 18.6, L 11.11]).
items.note: DiamondEtaleCohomology C4 constructs canonical compactifications; IG.3 proves the comparison.

items.name: Theorem 4.5.1 and Lemma 4.5.2 (the minimal fibre)
items.statement: f^* : Ig^{b,*}_C → (π*_HT)^{-1}(x) is an open immersion of affinoid perfectoid spaces with the same rank-one points; Ig^{b,tor}_C → Ig^{b,*}_C and (π^tor_HT)^{-1}(x) → (π*_HT)^{-1}(x) are isomorphisms on global sections (almost isomorphism O^{+a}/p^n → π_*O^{+a}/p^n via connected Stein fibres and the relative primitive comparison).
items.note: [Sch15, Thm 4.1.1], [BS22, Thm 1.17], [Sch17, Prop. 14.8, Cors 16.9–16.10], [Sch13, Thm 3.13]. IG.3: 'For minimal fibers prove the affinoid integral-section comparison and the required almost isomorphisms'.

items.name: Lemmas 4.6.2–4.6.3 (no boundary cohomology at ℓ^∞-level)
items.statement: For j_{Nℓ^∞} : S_{K(Nℓ^∞),Q̄} ↪ S^tor_{K(Nℓ^∞),Q̄}, F_ℓ → Rj_{Nℓ^∞,*}F_ℓ is an isomorphism, and H^i(Ig^{X,tor}_{K(Nℓ^∞)}, F_ℓ) ≅ H^i(Ig^X_{K(Nℓ^∞)}, F_ℓ).
items.note: [Pin92, §2.7]: R^ij_* of the normal-crossing boundary are exterior powers of the local Kummer classes and the ℓ-power transition maps kill them. IG.4 plans this 'ℓ-power-level boundary-killing argument'.

items.name: Theorem 4.6.1 = Theorem 2.8.3 (semiperversity)
items.statement: Every geometric point of Fℓ_C has a cofinal system of affinoid étale neighbourhoods U = Spa(A) with 𝔘 = Spf(A°) such that Rψ(Rπ°_HT*F_ℓ)|_𝔘 ∈ ^pD^{≥d}(𝔘_k, F_ℓ), d = [F^+ : Q]n^2.
items.note: Via ℓ^∞-level, [Sch15, Thm 4.1.1] affinoid perfectoid preimages from finite level, an integral mod-p map satisfying the valuative criterion (as [CS17, Prop. 6.1.3]), t-exactness of nearby cycles [Ill94] and [Hub96, Thm 3.5.13]. IG.4 proves CSnc Theorem 4.6.1.

items.name: The setup of §5.1 and semisimple Langlands parameters (Remark 5.1.1)
items.statement: p split in F_0 ⊂ F, F^+ ≠ Q, S ⊃ {∞} ∪ primes dividing pℓΔ_F and the ramification of a character ϖ : A^×_{F_0}/F_0^× → C^× extending the quadratic character of F_0/Q; T^S over q ∈ Spl_{F_0/Q} ∖ S with T_{i,v}; J_b(Q_p) ≅ J_{b_v}(F_v) × ∏ J_{b_w}(F_w) × Q_p^× with J_{b_v} an inner form of a Levi of GL_{2n}(F_v), whose irreducible representations have semisimple L-parameters σ_{π_v} ([Bad07]); the semisimple parameter of a Frobenius-semisimple WD representation is its restriction along w ↦ (w, diag(|w|^{1/2}, |w|^{−1/2})).
items.note: ET.4 (the CSnc normalizations, the character of F_0/Q) and ET.6 (GL_m and its inner forms). The double coset of T_{i,v} is printed over w | 𝔭 for w | 𝔮 (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: Theorem 5.1.2 (Galois representations for the constituents of Igusa cohomology)
items.statement: Let N be divisible by the N_0 of Remark 5.4.5 (supported in S^p_f = S_fin ∖ {p}) and [H_c(Ig^b_{K(N)}, Q̄_ℓ)] = Σ_j n_jπ_j ⊗ ψ_j. For each j there is a continuous semisimple ρ_j : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_{2n}(Q̄_ℓ), unramified at v | q ∉ S split in F_0 with characteristic polynomial X^{2n} − ψ_j(T_{1,v})X^{2n−1} + … + q_v^{n(2n−1)}ψ_j(T_{2n,v}), and for v | p the semisimple Langlands parameter of π_{j,v}|·|^{1/2−n} is that of ρ_j|Gal(F̄_v/F_v).
items.note: ET.7b (rational Igusa trace comparison) with AG2.2/AG2.5 for the Galois representations; IG.5 applies it.

items.name: Endoscopy for the unitary similitude group (§5.2)
items.statement: The quasi-split groups G_n⃗ ([Shi11, §3.1]) with G_n⃗(R) = {(λ, g) : gΦ_n⃗ ᵗg^c = λΦ_n⃗}, G_Q ≅ G_{2n}; representatives (G_{2n}, 1, id) and (G_{n_1,n_2}, (1, (I_{n_1}, −I_{n_2})), η_{n_1,n_2}) of E^ell(G), excluding n_1, n_2, [F^+:Q] all odd ([Kot84, 7.4.3]); L-groups and the L-morphisms η̃_{n_1,n_2} built from ϖ, ǫ(m) ≡ m mod 2 and N(n_1, n_2) = [F^+:Q](n_1ǫ(n_1) + n_2ǫ(n_2))/2 (after [Rog92, §1.2]).
items.note: ET.4: 'For CSnc's G_(n_i), build the finite-place transfer maps … and prove all commuting diagrams of L-morphisms'.

items.name: Definition 5.3.1 and Theorem 5.3.2 (Shin's stable trace formula for Igusa varieties)
items.statement: For acceptable φ = φ_p · 1_{K(N)} · φ^S ([Shi09, Def. 6.2]) with transfers φ^n⃗ (Shin's φ^n⃗_p [Shi10, §6], Langlands–Shelstad at S^p_f, η̃^*_n⃗ on H^ur, Euler–Poincaré functions at ∞): tr(φ | H_c(Ig^b, Q̄_ℓ)) = Σ_{G_n⃗} ι(G, G_n⃗)ST^{G_n⃗}_e(φ^n⃗).
items.note: ET.5 proves Shin's stable Igusa identity (no ker^1 factor here by Proposition 2.1.2).

items.name: Base change for 𝒢_n⃗ and compatibility of transfers (§5.4)
items.statement: 𝒢_n⃗ = Res_{F_0/Q}(G_n⃗ × F_0) with its L-group, BC_n⃗ and ζ̃_{n_1,n_2} with the commutative diagram (5.4.1); for v ∉ S the transfers BC^*_n⃗ and ζ̃^*_n⃗ with diagrams (5.4.2) of functions and (5.4.3) of unramified representations ([Shi11, (4.18)]); Remark 5.4.1: ζ̃^*(f_v) = f_v^{Q_{n_1,n_2}}·χ_{ϖ,v} and ζ̃_*(Π_v) = n-Ind(Π_v ⊗ χ_{ϖ,v}) ([Shi11, L 3.3]); BC-transfer at p (surjective) and at ∞ via Labesse's Lefschetz functions [Lab91].
items.note: ET.4.

items.name: Proposition 5.4.2, Lemmas 5.4.3–5.4.4 and Remark 5.4.5 (base-change transfer at bad places and the level N_0)
items.statement: If the stable orbital integrals of φ^n⃗ vanish off norms, φ^n⃗ is a BC-transfer ([Lab99, Prop. 3.3.2]); a semisimple element of G_n⃗(Q_v) is a norm iff its image in D_n⃗ = G_n⃗/G_n⃗^der is (after [Mor10, L 8.3.6]); hence for v ∈ S^p_f every φ_v supported near 1 has transfers φ^n⃗ that are BC-transfers, and N_0 is chosen so that K(N_0) is small enough at all v ∈ S^p_f.
items.note: [Mor10, L 8.4.1–8.4.2]. ET.4: 'Prove existence of the small bad-place level N_0 whose supported test functions satisfy the required transfer condition'. The proof of Lemma 5.4.3 writes Q_p for Q_v (sourceIssues E5).

items.name: Proposition 5.5.1, Definition 5.5.2, Lemma 5.5.3 and Remark 5.5.4 (the twisted trace formula without cuspidal subgroups)
items.statement: With 𝒢^+_n⃗ = (Res_{F_0/Q}G_m × Res_{F/Q}GL_n⃗) ⋊ {1, θ} and the invariant twisted trace formula (5.5.1): for BC-matching f^n⃗, φ^n⃗ with Lefschetz functions at ∞, I^{𝒢_n⃗θ}_geom(f^n⃗θ) = Σ_γ SO_γ(φ^n⃗) = τ(G_n⃗)^{-1}ST^{G_n⃗}_e(φ^n⃗). A cuspidal group has an R-anisotropic maximal torus modulo A_M; for [F^+:Q] ≥ 2, 𝒢_n⃗θ has no proper cuspidal subsets, so only 𝒢_n⃗θ contributes ([Art88b, Thm 7.1(b), Cor. 7.4], [Art88a, Prop. 9.1, Cor. 8.3], [Mor10, Prop. 8.2.3], [Lab99, Thm 4.3.4, Thm A.1.1]); for F^+ = Q, (Res_{F/Q}G_m)^s × G_{2(n−s)} are cuspidal.
items.note: ET.4: 'Prove that [F^+:Q]>1 rules out the proper cuspidal twisted subsets'. θ is printed with g^♯ = Φ_n⃗ ᵗg^c Φ_n⃗^{-1}, missing the inverse (sourceIssues E6).

items.name: Theorem 5.6.1, Lemma 5.6.2 and Remark 5.6.3 (the Igusa trace through θ-stable representations)
items.statement: tr(φ | [H_c(Ig^b, Q̄_ℓ)]) = τ(G)Σ_{G_n⃗} ǫ_n⃗ I^{𝒢_n⃗θ}_spec(f^n⃗θ) (ǫ = ½ for n⃗ = (n, n)); it is a linear combination of tr(Red^b_n⃗(π^n⃗_p)(φ_p)) · tr((Π^n⃗)_{S^p_f}(f^n⃗_{S^p_f}) ∘ A) · tr((ζ̃_n⃗*Π^n⃗)^S((f^{2n})^S)) with Π^n⃗ θ-stable isobaric, cohomological at ∞, for every φ_p (acceptability removed by [Shi09, L 6.4]); several n⃗ may contribute the same character.
items.note: ET.7b (with Red^b from [CS17, §5.4] and [CS17, L 5.4.2]). The proof cites 'Section of [Shi11]' without a number (sourceIssues E7).

items.name: Theorem 5.7.1 (Galois representations for the pieces Π_i)
items.statement: Writing Π^n⃗ = ψ ⊗ Π_1 ⊗ Π_2 on 𝒢_{n_1,n_2}(A) = A^×_{F_0} × GL_{n_1}(A_F) × GL_{n_2}(A_F), there is ρ_i : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_{n_i}(Q̄_ℓ) with WD(ρ_i|Gal(F̄_q/F_q))^{F-ss} ≅ ι_ℓ^{-1}rec(Π_{i,q}|det|^{(1−n_i)/2}) at every place ([HT01] normalization).
items.note: From [MW89], [Shi11], [CH13], [Car12] for regular L-algebraic conjugate self-dual cuspidal pieces ([BG14]). AG2.2/AG2.5. The proof refers to 'Theorem 5.5.3 of [CS17]', the arXiv v1 numbering of the published Theorem 5.5.4 (sourceIssues E8).

items.name: Boundary strata of Ig^{b,*} by rational parabolics (§6.1)
items.statement: ∂Ig^{b,*} = ⊔_{[P]} Ig^{b,*}_{[P]} over the classes of the maximal parabolics P_r = Stab(0 ⊂ F^r ⊂ F^{2n−r} ⊂ F^{2n}), r = 1, …, n (preimages of the S_Z with rk X = r); limits over tame levels Ig^b_∞ etc.; compactly supported cohomology of schemes with integral maps to finite type ones ([Ham19]); X_r the symmetric space of GL_r(F ⊗ R); a symplectic filtration Z_b with Z_{b,−2} ≅ Hom(O_F^r, µ_{p^∞}), P_b(Q_p) ⊂ J_b(Q_p) and X_P with G_{2(n−r)}-structure.
items.note: IG.6 ('construct the filtration of the polarized p-divisible group and the lower-rank Igusa datum b_P'). The paper writes X_P = Z_{b,−2}/Z_{b,−1} (sourceIssues E9).

items.name: Theorem 6.1.1 (Pink's formula for Igusa varieties)
items.statement: RΓ_c(Ig^{b,*}_{∞,[P]}, i^*_{[P]}Rj_*F_ℓ) ≅ Ind^{J_b(Q_p)×G(A^p_f)}_{P_b(Q_p)×P(A^p_f)} RΓ(GL_r(F)\(X_r × GL_r(A_{F,f})), F_ℓ) ⊗ RΓ_c(Ig^{b_P}_∞, F_ℓ), J_b(Q_p) × G(A^p_f)-equivariantly, with P_b(Q_p) × P(A^p_f) acting through its Levi quotient.
items.note: IG.6 exports exactly CSnc Theorem 6.1.1.

items.name: The comparison map: parabolic induction, cup products and the map to the locally symmetric space (§6.2)
items.statement: Ig^{b,*}_{∞,[P]} → J_b(Q_p)/P_b(Q_p) × G(A^p_f)/P(A^p_f) realizes the induction; the map is the cup product of RΓ_c(Ig^{b_P}_∞) → RΓ_c(Ig^{b,*}_{∞,P}) (Theorem 3.3.15) and RΓ(GL_r(F)\(X_r × GL_r(A_{F,f}))) → RΓ(Ig^{b,*}_{∞,P}, i^*_PRj_*F_ℓ), the latter from the continuous map from the punctured perfectoid neighbourhood |Ig^b_{∞,P}| to GL_r(F)\(X_r × GL_r(A_{F,f})) given by the logarithms of the norms of the Poincaré-bundle sections of the Raynaud extension, with [Hub96, Cor. 3.5.14] and Borel–Serre (footnote 18).
items.note: IG.6: 'Construct the map of complexes as a cup product of the smaller Igusa factor and the arithmetic GL_r factor, using its embedding in the punctured formal neighborhood'. The text calls both maps P_b(A^p_f) × G(A^p_f)-equivariant (sourceIssues E10).

items.name: Proposition 6.3.1 and Remark 6.3.2 (the local computation)
items.statement: For the Igusa cusp label Z̃ of X, RΓ_c(Ig^{b_P}_∞, F_ℓ) ⊗ colim_{Γ⊂GL_{O_F}(X)} RΓ(Γ, F_ℓ) → RΓ_c(Ig^{b,*}_{∞,Z̃}, i^*_Z̃Rj_*F_ℓ) is an isomorphism ([Pin92, Thm 4.2.1], [LS18a, Thm 4.3.10, L 4.3.2]); the same method proves Pink's original formula Hecke-equivariant, an alternative to [Pin92, §4.8].
items.note: IG.6: 'Prove by toroidal local computation that the map is an isomorphism'.

items.name: Lemmas 6.4.2–6.4.3 (Hecke algebras of parabolics and Levis, after Newton–Thorne)
items.statement: RΓ_cont(K^S, Ind^{G(A^S)}_{P(A^S)}(−)) ≅ r_P^*RΓ_cont(K^S_P, −) on D^+_sm(P(A^S), F_ℓ), and r_M^*RΓ_cont(K_M, −) ≅ RΓ_cont(K^S_P, Inf^{P(A^S)}_{M(A^S)}(−)) on D^+_sm(M(A^S), F_ℓ), with r_P restriction of functions and r_M integration along unipotent fibres ([NT16, §§2.2.3–2.2.4, Cors 2.6, 2.8, L 2.1, 2.4]).
items.note: IG.6 ('actual Hecke polynomial factorization'); IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.2 (Hecke algebras acting on complexes). The Levi is written Res GL_r × G_{n−r,Q} (sourceIssues E11).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 6.4.1 (length at least three from the boundary)
items.statement: By induction on n: a failure of H_{c−∂} → H at m forces (6.4.3) at m^∨ for some [P_r]; Theorem 6.1.1 and Lemmas 6.4.2–6.4.3 pull m^∨ back along the unnormalized Satake transform to m_1 ⊗ m_2 for GL_r/F and G_{2(n−r)}, whose Galois representations ([Sch15, Cor. 5.4.3] or [ACC+23, Thm 2.3.5]) give ρ_m with three summands when r < n; P_n contributes no stratum unless b is ordinary; otherwise concentration and Theorem 5.1.2 finish.
items.note: IG.6. The last step cites 'Proposition 2.8.4 and Corollary 2.8.2' for Lemma 2.8.4 and Proposition 2.8.2 (sourceIssues E12).

items.name: Poincaré duality for X_K and for Igusa varieties with dual Hecke ideals
items.statement: H^i_c(X_K, F_ℓ)_m is dual to H^{2d−i}(X_K, F_ℓ)_{m^∨} ([ACC+23, Prop. 2.2.12, Cor. 2.2.13]); likewise for Igusa varieties at finite level.
items.note: EDC.2:pairings; IG.5/IG.7 track the dual ideal.
